Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anand Prakash Dubey,G.A.,Prashant Kumar Dubey
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
Compliance affidavit filed by learned A.G.A. is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Manu Raj Singh, learned Advocate holding brief for Sri Avanish Kumar Srivastava,
counsel for the applicant and Sri Anand Prakash Dubey, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri A.K. Tripathi, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 29 of 2024, U/S 376(3), 506 IPC and 5N/6 POCSO Act,
Police Station Jani, District Meerut, during the pendency of trial.
PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The FIR was instituted by the wife of the applicant stating that her marriage was solemnized with Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34432619/

sentences.text: After discord, the informant is stated to have gone to her maternal home at Lucknow, leaving behind her estranged husband and three siblings (two daughters and a son).
5. On 28.1.2024, she returned to her husband's house, and was told by her minor daughter aged about 14 years that the applicant had raped her during the period from 15.1.2024 to 26.1.2024.
The said fact was narrated to her father by the informant.
6. On 29.1.2024 at about 11.00 am, when the informant was on the roof of the house, her husband forcibly dragged her daughter to his room.
On hearing her shrieks, she went down and saw that her daughter had assaulted the applicant with a stick (danda) to save herself.
The informant had gone alongwith her daughter (victim) to the police station.
The FIR was instituted on 29.1.2024 at 3.20 pm.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE APPLICANT:
7. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
8. The FIR is delayed by three days since the last date of offence committed with the victim.
9. The statement of the informant is an improvement to the FIR, as it is stated therein that she had gone to the house of the applicant alongwith her father.
The name of the father has been introduced later on.
10. The statement of the victim recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and by the doctor conducting her medical examination
is self-contradictory, as it is mentioned therein that the applicant had raped her and had told her not to reveal the matter to anybody, otherwise he would poison her.
The statement of the victim recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. categorically states that she used to talk to a neighbour Rahul on phone and the matter came to the knowledge of the applicant (her father).
The victim has been raped by the applicant stating that he shall foist the said case of rape on neighbour Rahul.
11. The statement of victim reveals that she was raped for the first time on 15.1.2024 at about 3.00 pm and again in the night and the same was repeated several times.
Her father and mother used to fight with each other and the matter was settled between the two.
The daily expenses of her mother are borne by her maternal grand-father.
12. There are further allegations that the applicant had shown her certain indecent photographs of her mother also.
The victim has stated that she had gone to school during the said period, but had not revealed the matter anywhere.
The presence of the brother of the informant has also been introduced in the said statement.
13. The statement further reveals that on 24.12.2023, the neighbour Rahul had sent a message on the mobile of the applicant, as such, she was scolded by the applicant.
The said fact has not been mentioned in the FIR.

sentences.text: 14. The informant carries animosity to applicant, which is but evident from the fact that the informant had left the house of the applicant without informing anybody earlier on, and the said matter was reported to the Director General Police, Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow, by the father of the applicant on 9.10.2012.
The matter was settled between them on 4.11.2012, which has been mentioned in the application given by father of the applicant at police station PGI, Lucknow on 4.11.2012.
The informant did not follow family traditions, as such, after much persuasion, a compromise was entered into between the applicant and the informant.
The said compromise has been filed as Annexure-10 to the affidavit.

15. There are the statements of the two other siblings of the applicant, who happened to be the real sister and brother of the victim, who have categorically denied the victim being subjected to any kind of sexual assault by the applicant.
It is mentioned by them that the informant wanted to take the victim to her maternal home at Lucknow, as such, the instant FIR has been instituted.
They have also stated that the applicant used to love all the three children equally.
16. The brother of the victim has stated that he had seen the victim talking to the neighbour Rahul on phone and had told the said fact to his father.
The applicant being a responsible father, had scolded the victim to refrain from talking to the neighbour, as she was of tender age.
17. The victim herein is a bright student.
The documents pertaining to her education have been filed with the rejoinder affidavit as RA 1.
Taking the victim away would have put an adverse effect on her education.
Her age in it is mentioned as 28.2.2008, although it is argued that the age is immaterial in the instant case but she was nearing her age of majority.
As per the ossification test report, the age of the victim has come out to be 18 years, which may vary by two years on either side.

18. Learned counsel has placed reliance on the medical examination report of the victim, which categorically indicates that the date of her last menstrual period was 15.1.2024, as such, there was no possibility of the offence being committed to her on that date.
Learned counsel has also referred several parts of the said medical report but they are being withheld to avoid prolixity.
19. To avoid verbiage certain facts relating to the medical evidence are not being mentioned here.
20. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
21. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 31.1.2024 and no witness has been examined to date.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/STATE:
22.

The medical report indicates that the victim had injuries sustained on her body, as a bluish contusion was found behind her ear and some injury marks were found on her chest, as such, she Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34432619/
3 was subjected to sexual assault by the applicant.

sentences.text: 23. The applicant herein is the father of the victim and has misused his clout and the said relationship.
The relation of father and daughter is the most pious one and he has broken the said trust of the victim.

ARGUMENTS IN REBUTTAL ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
24.

In rebuttal, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that there is no allegation either in the FIR or in the statement of the victim recorded u/s 161 or 164 Cr.P.C. of any kind of assault on her by the applicant on the body parts, where old injuries have been observed.

CONCLUSION:
25. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.
26.

A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
27.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
28. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
29. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

30. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, the medical report of the victim, statements of the brother and sister of the victim and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

31. Let the applicant- Sunil Kumar involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34432619/
4 court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

entities.text: Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
32. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

33. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
